entities.summary: Abū Manṣūr Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Azharī, known as Abu Mansur al-Azhari, was a prominent Arabic lexicographer and philologist of the 10th century. Born in unknown location, he spent most of his life in Baghdad, where he became a prominent figure in the translation of Greek and Persian texts into Arabic. His magnum opus, Tahdhib al-Lughat, is a comprehensive dictionary of Arabic that would go on to shape the language for centuries to come. Abu Mansur al-Azhari's work on philology and linguistics had a profound impact on the development of Arabic literature and culture, influencing scholars such as Ibn Rushd and Ibn Sina. His legacy extends beyond the medieval period, with his work remaining an essential reference for modern scholars of Arabic language and literature. Abu Mansur al-Azhari's contributions to the field of linguistics are still celebrated today, with his dictionary being translated into numerous languages and remaining a standard reference for scholars of Arabic language and literature.
